event.summary: Container dial staging disables its process-exit diagnosis
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04ffdbb35773cef36e73eb798c005ddbeb9a9de6. Also confirmed present at 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b (manager.rs:4268 and 5381). TLDR: when SSH refuses a container connection because its container host has reached its session limit, Farhelm reports a generic wait-for-hello failure instead of explaining the container host's SSH session limit. Other pre-helper container process exits similarly miss their intended diagnosis. Source route: SystemTransport::connect introduced in 1038bb1f4549f6896fa6e064fecf540f4548b4da creates Some(SshDiagnostics) for every RemoteRoute, including PodmanExec, and records ProcessRoute::LocalPodman or NestedSsh (transport.rs:228-235, 387-404, 650-692). At 04ff, HostKind::ssh_access explicitly returns None for Podman (store.rs:886-890). manager::HostActor::dial still interprets None as proof that no process marker exists and immediately advances to WaitingForHello (manager.rs:4143-4147), before observing a marker. ssh_failure_detail permits process-exit classification only at ConnectingToHost (manager.rs:5256); both the nested session-limit branch (5262-5270) and local exec exit branch (5258-5260) are consequently unreachable for real container dials. The raw bounded stderr may still include the mux refusal, but the explanatory container-host/session-limit diagnosis is suppressed. Contract: SPEC_impl.md, One route for transport and provisioning, says 'When the fallback login fails, launch refusal or connection unavailability names the container host’s SSH session limit.' The source also documents that marker or successful-hello evidence, not transport kind alone, outranks exit evidence (manager.rs:5237-5242). Suggested fix: stage by the actual TransportConnection process diagnostics (or an exhaustive process-transport predicate), advancing immediately only for a socket transport; retain ConnectingToHost until the process marker for Podman exec. Suggested bucket: other (diagnostic correctness; source establishes no lost work or credential exposure). Confidence: confirmed by source and contracts, not execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none, coverage sources not consulted. Caveats: provisioning launch setup's separate nested_session_failure classification at 566 is unaffected, and unit-level classifier tests can bypass the erroneous actor staging by supplying ConnectingToHost directly. No runtime reproduction or test was run.

event.summary: Process transport keeps cancellation ownership without a drainer cycle
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1038bb1f4549f6896fa6e064fecf540f4548b4da. Discovery pass 1. TLDR: considered whether generalizing SSH connections to Podman child processes leaves a transport child or its stderr drainer alive through a hidden ownership cycle after the connection is cancelled. Source refutation: process_connection (transport.rs:655-692) gives the reader and SshDiagnostics the ProcessLifetime anchors. relay_process_stderr receives only SshObservation, whose fields are bounded state, watch sender and Notify, without a child or lifetime anchor (438-455). Dropping the final lifetime aborts the stderr task and drops the kill_on_drop child (325-335), even if another process holds the stderr pipe. The writer does not create a reverse Arc edge. Compared the complete transport diff from exclusive-range base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a to this revision: this ownership algorithm is retained with renamed lifetime/channel helpers; the route metadata is assigned synchronously before spawning the drainer. This checks attribution across the range, not just against the selected commit parent. Contract: SPEC_impl.md One route for transport and provisioning assigns byte-stream/stderr/child ownership to the connection, and separately requires the environment helper watchdog because closing a Podman exec client need not end its inner helper. No claim is made that killing the client synchronously kills every remote descendant; the 120-second helper bound is the explicit contract already recorded in c2. Suggested bucket: other for a transport child/drainer leak if established. Could-be-highest: no established user-work loss or security route; the suspected resources are the connection helper and drainer. Confidence: confirmed source refutation, no execution. proposed_drop: true, no lifetime cycle or new cancellation gap found in the assigned transport change. possible_cover: none searched. Original considered consequence is orphan transport resources after cancellation; no runtime occurrence alleged.
